name: Opal
author: Martin Boyd

provenance.from: Ultimate Amiga forum, AMOS Factory downloads section, retrieved 2026-07-26. Most items there are credited "provided and archived by Lonewolf10". Archive path: Opal_1.1. The `devdocs/` subtree is Opal Technology's own developer kit, `driver/video/devdocs.lha` on Aminet, uploaded 22 September 1993 -- the AutoDocs, the hardware manual, the include files, the FD file and `opal.library` v4.3 itself. Its `AMOS/` directory holds `Opal.lib`, `Opal.s` and `Opal.Readme` byte for byte identical to the files already here, which is how the two are known to be one publisher's.
provenance.note: Documentation coverage was measured by counting how many of the library's own keyword names appear in the files shipped beside it, taking only files that can be documentation (not disk images, example programs or the library itself). That measures the DOCUMENTATION, which is what the `docs` field records; it does not set the evidence tier, which follows from what is available to read. The extension's tier is SOURCE -- Opal.s is the whole shim -- and the library it calls is DOCUMENTED by its own AutoDocs with the binary present to settle whatever they leave open.
provenance.redistribution: Third-party extension, redistribution terms unverified unless stated in the notes. Kept as a fixture for identification and reference only.

findings: Drives the OpalVision 24-bit graphics card: 78 keywords, 77 ported. `Opal.s` ships too, and an earlier note dismissed it as a fragment on its size alone -- 1,003 lines for 78 keywords. It is the whole extension: every keyword has its own L_ label and routine body, and they are short because the extension is a thin shim, each one popping its arguments and tailing into `opal.library` through the A_CALLOPAL macro. The card and the library are modelled in src/amiga/opalvision.ts. THE PIXEL LAYOUT IS NOT WHAT THE MANUAL IMPLIES: an OpalVision plane holds two bits per pixel, four pixels to a byte, so 24-bit colour takes twelve planes and not twenty-four, doubled in hires because the even and odd pixels sit in different banks. No document in the kit says so; `WritePixel24` and `CreateScreen24` in the shipped binary do. Eight defects are pinned, three in the extension and five in the library, and every one is reproduced rather than fixed; src/runtime/opal.ts lists them. All 78 are ported. `Ovsavejpeg24` and the JPEG half of `Ovloadimage24` needed a codec rather than a keyword, and src/amiga/jpeg.ts is it: the library's JPEG code is the Independent JPEG Group's, v4-era, compiled with SAS/C into the library's fourth hunk, so the Annex K tables, the quality law, the 4:2:0 sampling and the marker order are all read off the binary rather than guessed. The forward DCT is this port's own, so output is a conformant baseline JPEG and not a byte-identical one. Slot from Andrew Burton's AMOS Extensions List (kept at ultimateamiga.com, updated 2007-07-29), compiled from the AMOS-LIST archives 1994-1998, Amiga magazine clippings and coverdisk CDs, and confirmed by the extension's own `ExtNb EQU 21-1`.
notes: Drives the OpalVision 24-bit graphics card: true-colour screens, pixels, sprites and dual display.
